projects.name: Dwell AI
projects.description: A public AI broker assistant for the Egyptian market, embedded in dwellegypt.com — a 19-tool agent that answers buy/sell questions, evaluates units, and compares projects while streaming its reasoning live. I built the chat experience and the AI backend integration.
projects.markdown_description:
Dwell AI is what happens when a brokerage opens its data to an LLM carefully. Embedded in dwellegypt.com, it acts as a public broker assistant: visitors ask whether to buy or sell, compare projects, evaluate a specific unit, or ask for current opportunities — and the assistant answers with grounded data, then hands qualified leads to the brokerage.

## A real agent, not a chat toy

The assistant runs a LangChain agent with **19 tools**: searching the unit inventory (through the same three-tier pricing expression the internal systems use), hydrating visual unit cards, pulling market intelligence sheets and developer rankings, reading broker insights, normalizing currencies, and creating leads. For developer questions it does RAG over developer documents — embeddings into a vector store, retrieved into context at answer time.

Recommendations are scored on an **8-pillar investment model** — Location, Delivery, Budget, Liquidity, Rental, Unit Quality, Developer, and Risk — with weights that shift depending on whether the visitor is buying a home or making an investment.

## Streaming people can trust

LLM features usually fail on feel: long silences, then a wall of text. Dwell AI streams over SSE with **seven typed progress phases** — understanding, extracting, searching, context, insights, scoring, composing — each with its own wait hints, so the UI always shows what the agent is doing. Answers render as sanitized markdown with zoomable media, and Arabic replies get proper RTL handling.

## The unglamorous parts that make it production

- **Semantic answer cache** so repeated questions are instant and cheap.
- **Per-message cost and latency analytics**, plus an OpenRouter trace (configured vs effective model, routing mode, prompt-cache hits) — unit economics on every reply.
- **Guest sessions with a free quota**, full accounts, and **shareable conversation links** that mint public read-only views.
- Structured tool modals — buy/sell intent, unit evaluation, project comparison, book-a-showing — that compile form input into precise prompts, so visitors who'd never write a good prompt still get a great answer.
- Per-message feedback and an admin analytics surface to watch it all.

I built the chat experience end to end: the streaming UI, the agentic tool flows, and the backend integration that keeps a consumer-facing LLM grounded, observable, and within budget.

projects.name: Wallets CRM
projects.description: The internal operating system of a working brokerage — CRM, property inventory, four AI assistants, market intelligence, commissions, and WhatsApp campaigns in one platform I designed and built over seven months. A private system; no public link.
projects.markdown_description:
This is the biggest thing I have built: the system a real brokerage runs its day on. Roughly **2,100 commits in under a year**, **~700 API endpoints**, and **~200 database tables** — CRM, inventory, AI, market intelligence, commissions, and campaigns, built almost single-handedly.

## Natural-language client search

The feature that gave the system its name. Agents search **175K+ client records** in natural language, backed by PostgreSQL trigram fuzzy matching and weighted full-text vectors, with phone normalization down to last-8-digits matching. Three modes — standard, inventory-scoped, and an AI mode that turns a sentence into a structured query — with permission-tiered rate limits.

## The CRM agents actually use

Starred clients and units, notes, interactions, tasks with feeds, week and month scheduling, pipeline tags, custom views, sales targets, and an AI "action board" that drafts the week's priorities. On the money side: active-deal and commission workspaces per agent and per team.

## Inventory with an honest pricing engine

A full hierarchy — developers, projects, phases, buildings, units — where every unit's price flows through a **three-tier hierarchy** (listing price → override → estimate) with confidence scores. Internal codes carry a ±% "temperature", and linked code groups propagate one adjustment across sibling codes with a full before/after audit log and exact undo. A satellite map of Egypt carries project, phase, and building overlays with georeferenced masterplans.

## Four AI assistants, one control panel

The platform runs four configurable assistants — a public broker assistant, a market analyst, a pipeline copilot, and a logs investigator — each with its system prompt and model editable from an admin screen. Recommendations are scored on an 8-pillar investment model; the public assistant is documented separately as Dwell AI.

## Market intelligence + campaigns

Structured developer risk assessments (weighted categories, critical flags) feed the AI's risk pillar. A primary-data pipeline ingests developer availability sheets through parser specs, batch review, and a unit-matching workspace. And a WhatsApp campaign system — templates, threads, scheduled dispatch — handles outreach where clients actually are.

## Security that proved itself

Device fingerprinting, session telemetry, per-user risk scores, and anomaly alerts with live bot detection. During a third-party technical review, the system flagged the reviewer's headless browser as automation within seconds — unprompted, it demonstrated itself.

Everything above is described at the architecture level; client data stays private, and all demos run on synthetic fixtures.

projects.name: EgyGPT
projects.description: The Egyptian Arabic ChatGPT — an AI chat platform that thinks and answers in Egyptian dialect, not translated English. RTL-first, multi-model, with Egyptian-aware prompting throughout.
projects.markdown_description:
EgyGPT answers a question no one else was asking seriously: what does AI sound like when it actually speaks Egyptian? Not Modern Standard Arabic, not translated English — the way people in Cairo actually talk. I designed and built the platform around that idea, and it's live today at egygpt.com.

## What it does

- **Chats with Egypt, in Egyptian** — streaming AI chat with guest access and full accounts, multi-model by design: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, and more from one localized place.
- **Assistant presets** — beyond the general assistant, tuned personas like a marketer and a business advisor, each with its own Egyptian-aware behavior.
- **Egyptian-aware prompting** — system prompts that enforce the dialect, understand Franco-Arabic (3araby), and know Egyptian prices, cities, food, and expressions.
- **Real-time awareness** — web search wired in, so current events get current answers instead of outdated ones.

## How it evolved

The first version was three services I built from scratch: a React RTL frontend, a Laravel API, and a FastAPI/LangChain AI service with SSE streaming. The product then evolved into a customized LibreChat fork — multi-model out of the box, with my own layer on top: assistant presets, admin-configurable Egyptian system prompts applied to every model, and a retrieval stack (MongoDB + pgvector) grounding answers in real data.

## Why it mattered

Dialect is a feature, not a translation problem. Getting an LLM to reliably answer in عامية مصرية — and to feel local doing it — taught me more about prompt engineering than any English-first project ever did. EgyGPT is also the flagship product of Odynza, my AI company, and the foundation of everything I build with agents today.

projects.name: Wallets — walletsproperties.com
projects.description: Egypt's first data-driven real-estate investment platform — curated opportunities underwritten with real numbers, a monthly PDF magazine, an academy, and a free deal-modeling engine anyone can use. I built it full-stack.
projects.markdown_description:
Most property marketing in Egypt runs on emotion. Wallets was built on a different bet: give investors the numbers, honestly computed, and they will keep coming back. I designed and built the whole platform — the public site, the CMS behind it, and the financial engine at its core.

## The platform

- **Curated opportunities, underwritten like deals.** Each listing carries a deal snapshot — price, price per square meter against the market average, discount — plus "Wallets Numbers": projected upside, target IRR, liquidity, and risk. No vibes, no hype.
- **A monthly magazine, published as designed PDF issues**, and a block-based academy where lessons are composed from rich text, charts, images, and videos through a custom editor.
- **Careers with application intake**, and a full admin CMS to run all of it.

## The Commercial Analysis engine

The centerpiece is a free, no-login deal underwriter. You describe a unit — price, area, payment plan with arbitrary down-payment schedule and installments over years, maintenance deposit, delivery date — pick a strategy (exit only, exit and rent, rent only, personal use), and it builds the full monthly cashflow series.

Under the hood it computes **IRR with a Newton–Raphson solver (bisection fallback)**, blended ROI on cash actually paid, NPV with a present-value summary, and even detects the month rent starts covering the installment. Assumption sets (conservative / base / aggressive) are admin-configurable. Every deal auto-saves, gets a shareable URL, and can be forked — which turned a tool into a quiet growth loop.

I also gave it an analytics backend designed for restraint: IPs are stored only as SHA-256 hashes with a daily-rotating salt, user agents are truncated, bots are flagged, and writes are rate-limited. A lead magnet didn't need to cost anyone their privacy.

## Stack

A single Bun process serving the API and the React 19 SPA, PostgreSQL via postgres.js, Tailwind 4, deployed on Railway. The schema self-heals at boot — idempotent DDL instead of a migration framework — which made solo-operating the platform dramatically simpler.

projects.name: Dwell — dwellegypt.com
projects.description: The public face of Dwell, a Cairo luxury real-estate brokerage — a React marketing platform whose every section is served live from the brokerage's ERP content API. I designed and built the frontend and its API integration end to end.
projects.markdown_description:
Dwell needed more than a website: the brokerage's story, people, locations, and open roles change constantly, and nobody on the team should ever have to touch code to update them. So I built dwellegypt.com as a fully content-driven platform — a React frontend that renders whatever the company's ERP says, section by section.

## What I built

- **A marketing site with zero hardcoded content.** Partners, heritage counters, office locations across Egypt and the UAE, the elite-experts roster, and testimonials all come from a versioned JSON API on the ERP. Edit a number in the CMS and it's live — no rebuild, no deploy.
- **A full careers pipeline.** Rich job postings (departments, salary ranges, employment types) rendered from the API, with an application flow that accepts resumes and lands them straight into the ERP's inbox, where HR works them through a status workflow.
- **Lead capture that respects the business.** The "Sell with Dwell" and contact flows distinguish form types, so a seller inquiry and a consultation request arrive pre-sorted, with fail-safe mail notifications.
- **Motion with intent.** A full-screen hero, animated counters, and scroll reveals — tuned to feel luxurious, not noisy.

## Engineering notes

React 19 + TypeScript (strict) + Vite 6 + Tailwind 4, React Router 7, and Radix primitives for the interactive pieces. The frontend never couples to the ERP at build time — it fetches everything at runtime, so the same build artifact serves any environment. Deployment is the pipeline I use across my projects: GitHub Actions builds the bundle and ships it over FTP to Hostinger.

The part I enjoyed most: the site's content API is consumed by more than the website — the company's voice assistant reads the same endpoints — so the schema had to be clean enough to be a genuine public contract, not an afterthought.

projects.name: Math Masr
projects.description: A live mathematics learning platform that gives students detailed lesson videos, study materials, assessments, and real-time support in one focused experience.
projects.markdown_description:
Math Masr is a working mathematics learning platform built around the full student journey: discover a course, study the lesson, use the supporting material, practise, and get help without leaving the product. It is live again at [mathmasr.com](https://mathmasr.com).

## Built around the study loop

The public landing experience makes the promise clear, then the student application takes over once a learner signs in. Every course is structured for the student's grade, and lessons can carry video, PDF material, availability, and access state.

- **Detailed explanation videos** give each lesson a clear teaching surface.
- **PDF and study material** support revision alongside the video.
- **Exams and homework** turn a lesson into active practice, with timed flows and feedback.
- **Personal real-time support** keeps the experience connected to the student rather than feeling like a static content library.

## What I built

I designed and built the public product entry point and the authenticated student experience behind it: course discovery, grade-aware lesson lists, lesson access and purchase states, content delivery, and online assessment flows. The platform pairs a React frontend with a PHP and SQL backend so the learning structure, content, and student activity all live in one system.

## Why it matters

Education products usually fail in the hand-offs: a polished marketing page, a separate video library, then a disconnected exam tool. Math Masr makes those steps one continuous experience — the student can move from explanation to material to practice in the same product.

projects.name: million pictures of love
projects.description: A location-first memory product where people turn a meaningful photograph into a place-bound keepsake they can share through an interactive map.
projects.markdown_description:
A photo can be beautiful anywhere. A memory becomes personal when it belongs to a place. Million Pictures of Love is a location-first memory product: people attach a photograph to the coordinates that give it meaning, then share that moment as a place on a map.

## The experience

The public landing page invites people into the map instead of a feed. From there, the creation flow guides a person through finding a meaningful location, dropping an exact pin, uploading and cropping an image, and sharing the finished memory.

- **Find the place** with Mapbox search, device location, or direct map movement.
- **Make the memory tangible** by pairing a photo with the exact point where the story happened.
- **Stay in control** with a personal gallery and an owner-controlled setting for whether map visitors can open a photo.
- **Share the moment** through a dedicated map view after publishing.

## What I built

I built the product experience across a React and TypeScript frontend and a PHP-backed service: the responsive marketing entry point, the Mapbox map interaction, image upload and crop flow, personal gallery, sharing journey, and the account-side controls around each posted photo. The result is deliberately not a conventional photo gallery; the map is the interface for discovering and revisiting stories.

## Design intent

The visual language is warm, editorial, and intentionally restrained so the photos remain the emotional centre of the product. The navigation stays out of the way, the map becomes the canvas, and the publishing path reduces a personal story to a few understandable steps.

## Screenshots

![Million Pictures of Love landing page — an invitation to save a relationship story at a real place](%%STORAGE_URL%%portfolio/files/million-pictures-home.png)

*The live entry point pairs the story with the map, not another scrolling feed.*

sections.title: About Nour
sections.body_markdown:
I build custom software systems for businesses — and I've been doing it since 2015. Not templates, not plugins: real systems, designed around how a business actually works, then built to run it day after day.

Along the way that's meant CRMs and ERPs running a working brokerage, education platforms used by real students (including one I built and now teach on myself), and AI agents that answer customers, search company data, and take over repetitive work — all live in production, not in demos.

The other half of my life is teaching: I teach 2nd-secondary students at language schools, on a platform I built myself. It keeps me honest — if I can explain it to a classroom, I can explain it to a boardroom. If you're building something, I'd love to hear about it.

sections.title: Learn programming the way it should be taught.
sections.body_markdown: In-person sessions, a workbook full of practice, and support that continues long after the lesson ends. Every tool in this course was built by your teacher — the platform, the workbook, even the AI that answers your questions.

sections.title: Your book has an AI now
sections.body_markdown: Every workbook comes with an AI assistant that answers only from your curriculum — nothing off-topic, nothing made up. Ask it anything from the book, anytime, and it explains the idea the way your teacher would. If a question is outside the curriculum, it politely says no.

sections.title: Seats are limited — join the next group
sections.body_markdown: Groups stay small on purpose, so every student gets real attention. Message me on WhatsApp to reserve a seat, or email anytime.

sections.title: Leen Edu — my own platform
sections.body_markdown: Every lesson is also recorded and published on Leen Edu, the education platform I built myself — so revision is always one click away. The same platform runs schools and instructors across Egypt, built by the developer of Leen Edu and Math Masr.

sections.title: What you get
sections.body_markdown: More than lessons — a complete system around them. In-person sessions, a printed workbook with answers a scan away, an AI assistant trained on your curriculum, quizzes that track your progress, scores sent home on WhatsApp, and recorded videos to revise anytime.

sections.title: How a session works
sections.body_markdown: Every session follows the same calm rhythm: we take attendance, warm up with a short quiz on the last lesson, learn the new material together, and finish by solving a group quiz as a team. After class, every student's scores reach their parents on WhatsApp.

sections.title: WhatsApp, always open
sections.body_markdown: Scores and progress reports arrive on WhatsApp after every quiz — students and parents always know exactly where things stand. Have a question between sessions? Send it anytime and it gets answered as soon as possible.

sections.title: The workbook
sections.body_markdown: About 100 questions for every lesson, across roughly 15 lessons — from gentle warm-ups to real exam-style challenges. Stuck on a question? Scan the QR code next to it and the answer opens on your phone, with the steps explained.

feedback.name: Fuad
feedback.quote:
I've worked with Nour for the last 2 months on an AI enhanced E-commerce website project. He's taken care of all of the work related to the Front-End and most of the Backend. Nour has been great at communication and collaboration to deliver the project. He was really reasonable when it came to iterating to achieve the desired quality. Working with Nour has been a pleasure and he has delivered high quality working website despite a few technical surprises that came up as a result of integrating with 3rd party APIs.
I would recommend Nour to anyone looking for a high quality full-stack developer.

feedback.name: Lance
feedback.quote:
Nour stands out for his diligent work ethic and receptive attitude. His swift response to changes and requests ensured the smooth progress my project. Working alongside Nour has been a pleasure, and I look forward to our ongoing partnership as he continues to contribute to the development of my project.
Without hesitation, I highly recommend Nour to anyone seeking a top-tier full-stack developer.
